items.claim: The opening seam warrant rests on a person shift that the bytes of 13:20 do not deliver at the verse opening, the woe-lexeme contrast carries a byte-false form label, and two byte-true catchwords straddle the row's own opening seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: (1) THE VARIANT SITS ON THE SEAM WARRANT. The two variant notes at 13:20 read ketiv שאי against qere שְׂא֤וּ and ketiv וראי against qere וּרְא֔וּ (oshb:Jer.13.20; the qere forms reach byte tier, the ketiv stands unpointed in the source). The ketiv pair are second-feminine-singular imperative forms, the qere pair second-masculine-plural, and the token standing between them is עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier), a masculine-plural suffix. So the claim that the address turns to a second-feminine-singular figure AT the opening of 13:20 holds only on the ketiv and is contested both by the qere and by that intervening suffix: under the qere the verse opens as a continuation of the masculine-plural address of 13:18 and the feminine singular arrives only mid-verse, at לָ֔ךְ and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier). The run actually spliced, הַבָּאִ֖ים מִצָּפ֑וֹן (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier), is a definite masculine-plural participle with a prepositional phrase and carries no addressee marking whatever, so it cannot support the person claim it is cited for. Recording the doubled note as consulted but not spliced does not disclose that the variant lies on the very forms the boundary rests on. (2) BYTE-FALSE FORM LABEL. The woe onsets at 22:13 and 23:1 are BARE and verse-initial: ה֣וֹי (oshb:Jer.22.13, byte tier) and ה֣וֹי (oshb:Jer.23.1, byte tier), each the first token of its verse. The vav-prefixed shape וְה֥וֹי (oshb:Jer.34.5, byte tier) is attested at exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, finals-normalized skeleton) -- 22:18 and 34:5, both funeral cries, neither a woe-oracle onset. Calling the 22:13 and 23:1 onsets vav-prefixed is contradicted by their own bytes. The oy digit itself is right (sweep: 8 verses, token-bound); a bare consonantal substring would instead return 14 verses by matching inside the enemy and fool nouns, so the token-bound object was correctly chosen. (3) UNDISCLOSED CROSS-SEAM COHESION. תִּֽפְאַרְתְּכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.13.18, byte tier) closes 13:18 and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) closes 13:20 -- only four verses book-wide carry that noun (sweep: 4 verses, finals-normalized skeleton) and two of them sit either side of the proposed seam; and עֵ֥דֶר (oshb:Jer.13.17, byte tier) is answered by הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier), a noun in six verses book-wide (sweep: 6 verses, finals-normalized skeleton). Two byte-true catchwords straddle the row's own opening seam and argue continuity with 13:17-13:19; they are precisely the support the fold-together alternative is left without. (4) The declared substrate signal naming a koh-amar speech formula has no basis in the span: none of the 153 koh-amar verses falls within 13:20-13:27, the nearest sites being 13:13 and 14:10. Parashah disclosure is itself accurate: setumah at 13:19 ahead of the opening and petuchah at 13:27 at the close (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets).

items.claim: The topical-header claim is byte-sound, but a ketiv/qere note inside the span goes undisclosed while the row makes a positive absence statement for the parashah layer.
items.evidence: VERIFIED FIRST: 14:1 opens verse-initially with אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.14.1, byte tier), and the header shape carrying the prophet's name is attested at exactly four verses -- 14:1, 46:1, 47:1, 49:34 (sweep: 4 verses, finals-normalized skeleton). Dropping the name from the needle widens the result to five verses by admitting the to-him variant in the superscription at 1:2, so the object and the digit are correctly bounded and the shape is not blended with the eleven-verse prose-sermon superscription shape. DEFECT: 14:3, inside the span, carries a variant note reading ketiv צעוריהם against qere צְעִירֵיהֶ֖ם (oshb:Jer.14.3; the qere reaches byte tier, the ketiv stands unpointed in the source). It is nowhere disclosed, while the row states positively that no verse within 14:1-14:6 carries a parashah mark -- true on the inventory -- and while variant notes at 13:20 and at 14:14 are disclosed in adjacent spans. One engaged disclosure layer owes the others across the span, and a positive absence statement for one layer beside silence on a present item in another is the asymmetry the disclosure rule exists to catch. SECONDARY: the appeal to how header-bounded units elsewhere carry their attached content as one piece is uneven across the four attested sites, since 46:1 heads a multi-chapter nations collection rather than bundling a description; the point needs a per-site read rather than one analogy.

items.claim: The plea's opening at 14:7 is byte-anchored verse-initially, the footing change cited is carried by the verse's own morphology, and span disclosure is complete.
items.evidence: 14:7 opens אִם עֲוֺנֵ֨ינוּ֙ עָ֣נוּ בָ֔נוּ (oshb:Jer.14.7, byte tier) as its first tokens, with first-common-plural marking in עֲוֺנֵ֨ינוּ֙ and בָ֔נוּ (oshb:Jer.14.7, byte tier) and second-masculine-singular direct address in עֲשֵׂ֖ה לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמֶ֑ךָ (oshb:Jer.14.7, byte tier) -- against 14:2-14:6, which is third-person description throughout with no addressee at all. The unit closes on the matching petition אַל תַּנִּחֵֽנוּ (oshb:Jer.14.9, byte tier), so the bounded communal cry described is byte-true at both ends rather than only at the opening. Disclosure is complete and accurate for the span: setumah at 14:9 at the row's own close, 14:7 and 14:8 unmarked, and 14:6 ahead of the opening unmarked (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets); no verse in 14:7-14:9 carries a variant note, so nothing is owed there. No byte-true device straddles either seam -- the drought vocabulary of 14:2-14:6 shares no token with the plea -- and no form-class label is asserted beyond what the pointed bytes carry.

items.claim: The one-verse boundary is defensible, but the frame-owner ground given for it is contradicted by the run the row itself splices and by the verse's third-person handling of the divine name.
items.evidence: The formula is where the row says it is: 14:10 opens כֹּֽה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה (oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier) as its first tokens, and the mouth is named, which the frame-ownership discipline requires. DEFECT 1: the ground stated for the seam -- that the pronouncement is spoken about the people rather than to them -- is contradicted by the continuation inside the same splice, לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier), a lamed phrase marking the people as the party addressed, which the row's own rendering also reads that way. The third-person forms pointed to (אָֽהֲבוּ֙, רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם, עֲוֺנָ֔ם, חַטֹּאתָֽם -- oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier) mark the oracle's SUBJECT, not its addressee, so subject person and addressee are conflated in the one sentence carrying the boundary. DEFECT 2: the verse carries no first-person divine clause at all and refers to the divine name in the third person inside the formula's own quotation -- וַיהוָה֙ לֹ֣א רָצָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier). Describing it as the deity answering the plea therefore over-specifies the mouth; first-person divine speech in this stretch begins only at 14:12 (אֵינֶ֤נִּי שֹׁמֵ֨עַ֙ and אָנֹכִ֖י מְכַלֶּ֥ה, oshb:Jer.14.12, byte tier), a contrast available in the bytes and unused. Disclosure is accurate: setumah at 14:9 ahead of the row and setumah at 14:10 itself (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), and no variant note falls on 14:10.

items.claim: The formula the row cuts on recurs verse-initially at 14:14 inside its own span, undisclosed, and the reason given for keeping that turn internal is contradicted by the bytes of 14:13-14:14.
items.evidence: The opening splice is sound: 14:11 begins וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.14.11, byte tier) verse-initially. DEFECT: the consonantally identical opening stands verse-initially again at 14:14 -- וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Jer.14.14, byte tier) -- and at 15:1 -- וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Jer.15.1, byte tier); the three differ only in accents. The shape is attested at 13 verses book-wide (sweep: 13 verses, finals-normalized skeleton). Nothing in the row discloses that the device carrying its own boundary recurs mid-span, while the same device is treated as decisive at the 15:1 onset. The reason stated -- that neither internal turn carries an addressee or scene change of its own -- is byte-false for 14:14: 14:13 is the prophet addressing the deity (וָאֹמַ֞ר אֲהָ֣הּ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה, oshb:Jer.14.13, byte tier) and 14:14 is the deity answering the prophet, which is exactly the relation treated as a seam where the plea addressed to the deity at 14:19-14:22 is answered at 15:1. On the bytes the two sites are the same shape in the same relation; either 14:14 is a seam or the criterion applied at 15:1 does not hold. Disclosure is otherwise complete and accurate here: setumah at 14:12, 14:13 and 14:14 within the span and at 14:10 ahead of it (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), and the doubled variant note at 14:14 -- ketiv/qere ואלול / וֶֽאֱלִיל֙ and ותרמות / וְתַרְמִ֣ית (oshb:Jer.14.14) -- is recorded; that note falls inside the lying-vision list and does not bear on the boundary, so leaving it unspliced is adequate there.

items.claim: The seam driver is a form-class misidentification -- the opening word of 14:17 is a waw-consecutive perfect, not an imperative -- and the same construction runs mid-verse at 15:2 with no boundary force.
items.evidence: DEFECT 1 (form class). 14:17 opens וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ (oshb:Jer.14.17, byte tier). Its pointing reads vav with sheva, alef with qamats, mem with patah, resh with sheva, and a final tav carrying dagesh and qamats -- the second-masculine-singular suffix-conjugation ending. The form is a waw plus perfect, not an imperative. The true second-masculine-singular imperative of this verb stands at 13:18, אֱמֹ֥ר (oshb:Jer.13.18, byte tier), with no such ending, and the imperative forms that actually open address units in this book are plurals of the type הַגִּ֣ידוּ ... הַשְׁמִ֔יעוּ (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier) and שִׁמְע֣וּ (oshb:Jer.10.1, byte tier). The pointing and the English rendering agree in reading a modal continuation rather than a command. A waw-perfect following divine speech can carry directive FORCE, but force is not form: the row asserts a form class and a discourse-frame device class, and the pointed bytes carry neither. No morphology layer is staged, so this is argued from the pointing and both witnesses' renderings. DEFECT 2 (not a seam device). The form is attested at 30 verses book-wide bare and at 18 verses with the following pronoun phrase (sweep: 30 verses and 18 verses, finals-normalized skeleton). One of those 18 is 15:2, where the same construction וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.15.2, byte tier) sits mid-verse inside a conditional as an ordinary continuation with no boundary function, four verses on in the same stretch. Grammatically 14:17 likewise continues the divine speech to the prophet begun at 14:14 and running through 14:16 rather than opening a fresh frame, and the row's own note that 14:16 is unmarked leaves the proposed seam without tier-3 corroboration as well. Not challenged: the typing decision and the mourning register are reasonable, the first-common-singular voice of the dirge is real (עֵינַ֥י, oshb:Jer.14.17, byte tier; יָצָ֣אתִי and בָּ֣אתִי, oshb:Jer.14.18, byte tier), disclosure is accurate (setumah at 14:18, 14:16 and 14:17 unmarked, single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), and no variant note falls in the span.

items.claim: The return to communal address at 14:19 is carried verse-initially by the bytes, and the pairing with 14:7-14:9 the row asserts is byte-true on a two-verse construction.
items.evidence: 14:19 opens הֲמָאֹ֨ס מָאַ֜סְתָּ אֶת יְהוּדָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.14.19, byte tier) as its first tokens, with second-masculine-singular address to the deity (מָאַ֜סְתָּ, נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ, הִכִּיתָ֔נוּ -- oshb:Jer.14.19, byte tier) and first-common-plural speakers (לָ֖נוּ, oshb:Jer.14.19; יָדַ֧עְנוּ, רִשְׁעֵ֖נוּ, חָטָ֖אנוּ, oshb:Jer.14.20; אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙, oshb:Jer.14.22 -- all byte tier) sustained to the close, a real footing change from the first-common-singular dirge voice of 14:17-14:18 (עֵינַ֥י, oshb:Jer.14.17, byte tier; יָצָ֣אתִי and בָּ֣אתִי, oshb:Jer.14.18, byte tier). The claimed pairing with the earlier plea is byte-true and tight rather than impressionistic: לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמֶ֑ךָ at 14:7 (oshb:Jer.14.7, byte tier) and לְמַ֣עַן שִׁמְךָ֔ at 14:21 (oshb:Jer.14.21, byte tier) are the only two verses in the book carrying that construction (sweep: 2 verses, finals-normalized skeleton). Disclosure is complete: setumah at 14:18 ahead of the opening and petuchah at 14:22 at the row's own close, 14:19-14:21 unmarked (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets); no verse in 14:19-14:22 carries a variant note. The forward boundary is handled consistently with the person evidence quoted: 15:1 is addressed to the prophet, not to the deity, so declining to absorb it follows from the same criterion used to open the row.

items.claim: A ketiv/qere note inside the span goes undisclosed in the very clause the row cites, and the span description merges two fourfold lists that the bytes keep apart.
items.evidence: The opening is sound: 15:1 begins וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י אִם יַעֲמֹ֨ד מֹשֶׁ֤ה וּשְׁמוּאֵל֙ לְפָנַ֔י (oshb:Jer.15.1, byte tier) verse-initially. DEFECT 1: 15:4 carries a variant note reading ketiv לזועה against qere לְזַֽעֲוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.15.4; the qere reaches byte tier, the ketiv stands unpointed in the source). It is undisclosed, although the row states positively that nothing within 15:1-15:4 carries a parashah mark -- true on the inventory -- and although variant notes at 13:20 and 14:14 are disclosed in adjacent spans. The omitted note sits inside the tossed-among-the-kingdoms clause that the row's own closing sentence cites, so it is directly span-relevant rather than incidental. DEFECT 2: the death, sword, famine and captivity assignment lies wholly inside 15:2 -- אֲשֶׁ֨ר לַמָּ֤וֶת לַמָּ֨וֶת֙ ... וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לַשְּׁבִ֖י לַשֶּֽׁבִי (oshb:Jer.15.2, byte tier), four pairs in one verse. 15:3 carries a DIFFERENT and separately numbered quartet, אַרְבַּ֤ע מִשְׁפָּחוֹת֙ (oshb:Jer.15.3, byte tier), whose members are sword, dogs, birds and beasts; the numeral occurs there and not in 15:2. Attributing one fourfold assignment of death, sword, famine and captivity to 15:2-15:3 conflates two distinct lists and attaches the numeral's home verse to the wrong one. ALSO UNREMARKED: the construction וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.15.2, byte tier), promoted to a discourse-frame seam driver at 14:17, recurs here mid-verse with no boundary force, which the span-internal reading does not address. Not challenged: the closure device is real -- 15:3 carries the postpositive נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.15.3, byte tier) -- and the koh-amar inside 15:2 is embedded in speech the prophet is told to deliver rather than a fresh divine onset, which the row correctly declines to treat as a seam.
